subject: On‑prem / VPC: key handover, data egress clauses, and BYOK handshaking
body_preview: Acme asks for firm language on data egress, BYOK handover, escrow and operator access windows; Redwood sends checklist and technical clarifications; Acme confirms and requests DPA addendum redline.
messages:
From: James Lee <security@acmetx.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: michael.grant@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem / VPC: data egress and BYOK handover questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme is moving quickly on a private deployment evaluation. Before we proceed to procurement we need a short, definitive writeup on a few items so our security and legal teams can greenlight the project: 

1) BYOK handover: what exact events trigger handoff of customer CMKs vs. Redwood retained keys? We need the contractual signal and an operational playbook (who signs off, how keys are rotated, breakglass process).

2) Data egress & operator access: if we run in our VPC/on‑prem colocation with your private control plane, under what circumstances would Redwood staff need to access plaintext data or model inputs/outputs? We need explicit limits and egress language for the DPA (e.g., "no operator access without prior written request except for scheduled maintenance with 14‑day notice").

3) Escrow/Key recovery: do you offer a keystore escrow option and what are the legal controls (escrow agent, access windows, notice, audit logs)?

4) Auditing evidence: sample telemetry or audit records we can receive (operator session logs, KMS audit events, retention window).

Can you respond with a short checklist and sample contract language by EOD tomorrow? If easier, a checklist PDF + a short technical note would be great.

Appreciate it — James

James Lee
Senior Security Engineer
Acme Therapeutics
security@acmetx.com

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: On‑prem / VPC: data egress and BYOK handover questions

James — thanks for the clear list. I've attached a concise checklist (redwood‑onprem‑egress‑checklist.pdf) that maps each ask to the operational control and the suggested DPA/DPA‑addendum language. High level answers below and then Prio (cc'd) will add the technical caveats.

Summary (short):
- BYOK handover: Customer controls CMKs; Redwood will never retain plaintext customer master keys. Handover triggers are (a) initial provisioning, (b) rotation with mutual auth, (c) termination. We propose a short clause that requires a written handover acceptance and a 7‑day rollback window on rotation.
- Operator access / data egress: Redwood's private control plane retains only metadata unless explicitly authorized. Operator access to compute nodes (where plaintext may be available during live debug) is limited to breakglass events documented + audit logs. Suggested contract language: "Operator access requires prior written authorization or documented incident ticket; emergency breakglass requires post‑facto notice within 24 hours and full session logs."
- Escrow: We support optional keystore escrow (third‑party custodian) for customers who request it; escrow release requires dual approvals (Redwood + customer legal) and an escrow agent SLA.
- Auditing evidence: We can provide KMS event streams (exported), operator session recordings, and periodic attestation reports.

Next steps: 
1) Prio — can you add the technical checklist & wording about access windows and the encryption-at-rest/in-transit guarantees?
2) Kimberly — legal, any immediate redlines to the suggested clause we should avoid?

I've uploaded the checklist and filled the questionnaire where it was straightforward; see attachments. If a short Zoom (30m) would help to align the contract language, we can set one up AM tomorrow.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Head, Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415 555 0136

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, James Lee <security@acmetx.com>
Cc: michael.grant@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem / VPC: data egress and BYOK handover questions

Thanks — adding the technical details. Quoting James' numbered items and responding inline: 

> 1) BYOK handover: what exact events trigger handoff of customer CMKs?

- Provisioning: Customer uploads CMK wrapping key material into a customer‑controlled HSM or KMS (BYOK). Redwood stores only the wrapped key reference and never has unwrapped key material. The contractual trigger is "customer uploads and acknowledges key fingerprint".
- Rotation: Customer initiates rotation via the control plane or issues an HSM rotation command. Redwood will apply rotated keys only after a signed rotation manifest (JWT signed with customer's operator key) or explicit acceptance in the control plane UI. There is a 7‑day rollback window during which previous key material is retained for recovery; after that, rotation is final.
- Termination/Offboarding: On termination, Redwood will zeroize any ephemeral key material and return wrapped key references; if escrow is enabled, the escrow agent will be invoked per the escrow SLA.

Suggested contract bullet: "Customer retains exclusive custody of CMKs. Redwood will not import or export unencrypted CMK material. Any rotation or handover requires a signed rotation manifest or documented handover acceptance."

> 2) Data egress & operator access: under what circumstances would Redwood staff need to access plaintext data?

- Normal ops: None. Model inference happens on customer‑controlled nodes; telemetry and metrics are aggregated in anonymized form.
- Debug / emergency: Operator access occurs only when the customer opens a support ticket with explicit consent or under a documented breakglass with 2 approvers (one customer, one Redwood). Access sessions are PSK‑based, timestamped, and streamed to an immutable audit log. Post‑access artefacts (session logs, command transcripts, any extracted traces) are delivered to the customer and purged per agreed retention.

Contract wording we recommend: "Redwood personnel will not access plaintext customer data except following documented customer authorization or emergency breakglass; all sessions will be recorded and delivered to the customer within 24 hours; operator sessions require two‑factor approvals as set forth in Schedule X."

> 3) Escrow/Key recovery: do you offer keystore escrow?

- Yes (optional). Escrow agent is an independent third party (we can propose two vendors). Escrow release requires dual approvals (legal teams from both parties) plus notarized release in extreme cases. Access windows are tight (typically 2 hours) and all actions are logged.

> 4) Auditing evidence: sample telemetry or audit records?

- We can provide: KMS audit export (JSON lines), operator session transcripts, system‑level attestation PDFs (signed), and a weekly activity digest. We can also offer S3 export of logs to an Acme‑owned bucket.

Operational caveats: network egress for certain kernel updates may contact Redwood mirrors. These are preapproved endpoints and can be allowed in the customer's firewall rules or sandboxed via an airgapped mirror. If Acme requires absolute zero egress, we can support a fully airgapped variant but that adds lead time and patching constraints.

I'll attach the micro‑playbook to the checklist (see attached). Happy to sync on a tech call tomorrow.

— Prio

Redwood Inference

Lauren / team — this is exactly what we needed, thank you. A few quick items: 

- The proposed contract bullets are fine from security's perspective. Legal asked that the breakglass definition include a 2‑hour emergency approval SLA and an explicit retention period for session logs (minimum 3 years).
- For escrow, please send vendor names and the proposed escrow agreement template — legal will run it and send a redline.
- We will accept the "7‑day rollback window" on rotations if it is explicitly called out in the DPA addendum.

Request: can you send a short DPA addendum draft (one page) that incorporates the operator access language, rotation rollback window, and escrow release controls? If you can point us at a DocuSign link for an initial head of terms, legal will start an internal review.

If you prefer to attach the draft, that works too. Zoom is not necessary; thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,

James
